answer: Moshi pairs the Helium text LLM with Mimi, a semantic-acoustic neural audio codec that encodes audio into discrete units for language modeling [Moshi: a speech-text foundation model for real-time dialogue, arXiv:2410.00037v1, PDF p. 41, §7 Conclusion]. The system utilizes a multi-stream architecture where the model predicts text tokens corresponding to Moshi’s speech and audio tokens for Moshi’s output, while ignoring the prediction of the user's audio stream in favor of actual input [Moshi: a speech-text foundation model for real-time dialogue, arXiv:2410.00037v1, PDF p. 17]. This streaming design claims a theoretical latency of 160 ms, which is lower than the 230 ms average observed in natural conversations [Moshi: a speech-text foundation model for real-time dialogue, arXiv:2410.00037v1, PDF p. 2, §1 Introduction][Moshi: a speech-text foundation model for real-time dialogue, arXiv:2410.00037v1, PDF p. 26].
question: Moshi keeps a text LLM and adds a smaller audio model. What does that audio model read and predict, and what theoretical latency does the streaming design claim against ordinary conversation?

This streaming design claims a theoretical latency of 160 ms, which is lower than the 230 ms average observed in natural conversations [[cite:35060eb5340b9d96]][[cite:d252558e81db180a]].
